messages:
Carmen Li: quick a11y pass on the new model-version timeline scrubber (the horizontal timeline we use to pick evaluation checkpoints). A couple of issues: keyboard scrubbing feels awkward and VoiceOver doesn't announce the timestamp while dragging.
Oren Feldman: good flag. Which interactions are failing? arrow keys, page keys, or drag with spacebar?
Carmen Li: arrow keys move fine but focus ring is tiny on dark theme and the handle isn't reachable by tab on Safari sometimes. When I drag with mouse, VO doesn't announce the updated time as the handle moves.
Priya Rao: slider-like components need role="slider" and the full aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow pattern. Are we using a div with mouse handlers? I think the current impl is a canvas + custom pointer handling.
Mika Tanaka: yes it's canvas for performance. Canvas is problematic for AT unless we mirror accessible controls. We should add a hidden <input role="slider"> or a real range input synchronized with the canvas position. That gives native keyboard support and AT announcements.
a11y-bot: automated-check: focus indicator thickness <3px flagged, contrast of scrubber handle (#6a6a6a) vs timeline bg (#1f1f1f) = 2.6:1 (fails AA), missing role=slider and aria attributes, live-region for updates missing.
Oren Feldman: plan: add an offscreen range input (input type="range") or an aria-hidden visual with an ARIA slider element positioned in DOM order. Sync value on PointerMove and update aria-valuenow. Also ensure the handle has visible :focus-visible style.
Carmen Li: preference for a native range input hidden visually but focusable, because it handles keyboard natively and VoiceOver will announce values. We'll style a separate visible handle for visuals and keep input in DOM for AT.
Priya Rao: if we use input[type=range], ensure we provide aria-valuetext with a human-friendly timestamp like "2026-02-12 14:23 UTC" and aria-labelledby referencing the visible label. Also add aria-live="polite" region that announces changes while scrubbing but debounce updates to avoid noise.
Mika Tanaka: minor nuance: VoiceOver on mac treats continuous live updates differently; better to announce the new value on commit (on pointerup) and while arrowing announce each step. For drag, many users expect continuous feedback, but it can be noisy. Debounce to 100-150ms and use aria-live politely.
Oren Feldman: for keyboard increments decide step size: left/right arrow = 1 checkpoint step, page up/down = 10, Home/End = min/max. Set input.step accordingly or handle programmatically and update aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow.
Carmen Li: accessibility for labels: add visible text "Checkpoint" and a sr-only description: "Use left/right arrows to move one checkpoint, PageUp/PageDown to jump 10." Put that into aria-describedby.
Priya Rao: don't forget to expose the current model version name in aria-valuetext when hovering a particular tick: e.g., aria-valuetext="v1.2.0 — 2026-02-12 14:23 UTC" so screen reader users get context.
a11y-bot: suggestion: ensure focus order places the slider early in the timeline region; also ensure the timeline ticks have role="option" or are reachable via keyboard if they are interactive. Color contrast for ticks against bg = 3.0:1; consider using --interactive-strong token.
Mika Tanaka: about visual focus: use outline: 3px solid var(--focus-accent) with outline-offset: 2px and only show via :focus-visible. That handles mouse vs keyboard.
Oren Feldman: we need a small code example to sync canvas timeline with an offscreen input. Draft:
```
// timeline-a11y.js
const input = document.querySelector('#timeline-range') // visible-hidden range
const canvas = document.querySelector('#timeline-canvas')
input.addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  const pos = valueToPosition(e.target.value)
  renderHandleAt(pos)
  liveRegion.textContent = formatValue(e.target.value) // debounced elsewhere
})
canvas.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e)=>{
  // calc value from pointer and set input.value then input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input'))
})
```

Carmen Li: perfect. Also add a11y tests: 1) cypress that tabs to slider and presses ArrowRight 3x and asserts aria-valuenow increased accordingly, 2) axe storybook snapshot for contrast and missing roles.
Priya Rao: testing notes: VoiceOver on mac will read aria-valuetext only when the slider receives focus or when value changes via keyboard. For drag events we should call input.setAttribute('aria-valuenow', value) and update live region to trigger announcement. Keep debounce 150ms for drag.
Mika Tanaka: UX question: do we announce updates while scrubbing or only on release? My vote: announce while using arrow keys (every step), and while dragging announce every 200ms max; on release give a final summary like "Selected checkpoint v1.2.0, 2026-02-12 14:23 UTC".
Oren Feldman: agreed. Implement debounce 200ms with final commit announcement on pointerup. Also ensure SR users can use Shift+Arrow for faster jumps (larger step). Document keyboard shortcuts in an sr-only hint.
Carmen Li: copy nit: use full timestamp plus timezone, avoid relative terms. e.g., "2026-02-12 14:23 UTC (v1.2.0)". Good for auditors.
a11y-bot: checklist: add role=slider or offscreen range input, aria-valuemin/max/now/text, aria-describedby with instructions, aria-live polite region debounced, focus-visible 3px, color tokens updated for handle & ticks, keyboard step mappings, cypress + storybook tests.
Priya Rao: last note: ensure the timeline is reachable by screen-reader rotor landmarks. Add role="region" aria-label="Model checkpoint timeline" so it's discoverable.
Mika Tanaka: I'll prototype the offscreen input approach and push a storybook with keyboard demo. Tagging @Oren for review on the value formatting and @Carmen for AT pass.
Carmen Li: thanks all. Assigning to @Mika to open draft PR with notes and tests. Will run VoiceOver + NVDA checks once PR is up. :thumbsup:
